chapters.verseRange: Verses 1.1 – 1.70 (70 श्लोक in the edition) · shown here: 1.20, 1.37
chapters.overview: Establishes the fundamental chronological coordinate system of Vedic astronomy. Decodes the 4,320,000-year Mahayuga, the exact solar civil days per cycle (1,577,917,828 days), Ahargana day-count summation, and mean planetary velocity vectors.

slokas.deva:
इत्थं युगसहस्रेण भूतसंहारकारकः ।
कल्पो ब्राह्मं अहः प्रोक्तं शर्वरी तस्य तावती ॥
slokas.translit:
itthaṃ yugasahasreṇa bhūtasaṃhārakārakaḥ ।
kalpo brāhmaṃ ahaḥ proktaṃ śarvarī tasya tāvatī ।।
slokas.translation: Thus a thousand yugas make the kalpa that brings about the dissolution of beings. That kalpa is called a day of Brahmā; his night is of equal length.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v1-20 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 1.20)

slokas.deva:
वसुद्व्यष्टाद्रिरूपाङ्कसप्ताद्रितिथयो युगे ।
चान्द्राः खाष्टखखव्योमखाग्निखर्तुनिशाकराः ॥
slokas.translit:
vasudvyaṣṭādrirūpāṅkasaptādritithayo yuge ।
cāndrāḥ khāṣṭakhakhavyomakhāgnikhartuniśākarāḥ ।।
slokas.translation: In a yuga there are 1,577,917,828 civil (sāvana) days and 1,603,000,080 lunar days (tithis). These two tallies are the backbone of the yuga calendar arithmetic.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v1-37 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 1.37)

chapters.overview: Rigorous non-Keplerian orbital perturbation calculus. Resolves true planetary positions through pulsating Manda (eccentricity) and Śīghra (synodic-anomaly) epicycles using variable circumference equations.

slokas.deva:
ओजयुग्मान्तरगुणा भुजज्या त्रिज्ययोद्धृता ।
युग्मे वृत्ते धनर्णं स्यादोजादूनाधिके स्फुटम् ।।
slokas.translit:
ojayugmāntaraguṇā bhujajyā trijyayoddhṛtā ।
yugme vṛtte dhanarṇaṃ syādojādūnādhike sphuṭam ।।
slokas.translation: Multiply the odd–even epicycle difference by the bhuja-jyā and divide by the trijyā; applied with the proper sign to the even-circle base (according as the true circle is less or greater than the odd-end value), this yields the sphuṭa (corrected) epicycle.

chapters.verseRange: Verses 3.1 – 3.51 (51 श्लोक in the edition) · shown here: 3.1, 3.2
chapters.overview: Trigonometric resolution of the 3 fundamental astronomical questions (Dik/Direction, Desha/Longitude, and Kala/Time) using the 12-digit Shankuyantra (gnomon), solar declination (Kranti), and equinoctial shadow (Palabha).

slokas.deva:
शिलातले अम्बुसंशुद्धे वज्रलेपे अपि वा समे ।
तत्र शङ्क्वङ्गुलैरिष्टैः समं मण्डलं आलिखेत् ।।
slokas.translit:
śilātale ambusaṃśuddhe vajralepe api vā same ।
tatra śaṅkvaṅgulairiṣṭaiḥ samaṃ maṇḍalaṃ ālikhet ।।
slokas.translation: On a stone surface cleaned with water—or even one finished with a hard vajra-plaster coating—made perfectly level, draw a circle whose radius equals the chosen number of aṅgulas of the gnomon.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v3-01 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 3.1)

slokas.deva:
तन्मध्ये स्थापयेच्छङ्कुं कल्पनाद्वादशाङ्गुलम् ।
तच्छायाग्रं स्पृशेद्यत्र वृत्ते पूर्वापरार्धयोः ।।
slokas.translit:
tanmadhye sthāpayecchaṅkuṃ kalpanādvādaśāṅgulam ।
tacchāyāgraṃ spṛśedyatra vṛtte pūrvāparārdhayoḥ ।।
slokas.translation: At the circle’s centre set a gnomon taken as twelve aṅgulas high. Note the points where the tip of its shadow meets the circumference in the eastern and western halves (of the day).
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v3-02 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 3.2)

formula.title: Ascensional Difference & Gnomon Equation
formula.notes: Determines local sunrise, daytime length (Dinamana), and the exact local sidereal ascendant (Lagna).

chapters.codeSnippet:
import math
def calculate_chara(lat_deg, dec_deg):
    sin_chara = math.tan(math.radians(lat_deg)) * math.tan(math.radians(dec_deg))
    sin_chara = max(-1.0, min(1.0, sin_chara))
    return math.degrees(math.asin(sin_chara)) * 4.0 # in minutes of time

Input: latitude 23.1765° N (Ujjain), solar declination +17.5°
calculate_chara(23.1765, 17.5) → +31.0308 minutes of time

chapters.nameEn: Lunar Eclipse Calculus & Shadow Cone Geometry
chapters.verseRange: Verses 4.1 – 4.26 (26 श्लोक in the edition) · shown here: 4.12
chapters.overview: Mathematical mechanics of lunar eclipses. Derives the apparent diameters of the Sun, Moon, and Earth's shadow cone (Bhamandala), contact times (Sparsha and Moksha), and totality duration (Sthityardha).

slokas.deva:
ग्राह्यग्राहकसंयोगवियोगौ दलितौ पृथक् ।
विक्षेपवर्गहीनाभ्यां तद्वर्गाभ्यां उभे पदे ।।
slokas.translit:
grāhyagrāhakasaṃyogaviyogau dalitau pṛthak ।
vikṣepavargahīnābhyāṃ tadvargābhyāṃ ubhe pade ।।
slokas.translation: Halve, separately, the sum and the difference of the eclipsed and eclipsing diameters. From those two squares, each diminished by the square of the latitude, extract both roots — the two “padas.”
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v4-12 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 4.12)

chapters.verseRange: Verses 5.1 – 5.17 (17 श्लोक in the edition) · shown here: 5.8
chapters.overview: Topocentric parallax calculus in longitude (Lambana) and latitude (Nati). Explains why solar eclipses are strictly localized phenomena differing fundamentally from lunar eclipses.

slokas.deva:
मध्यलग्नार्कविश्लेषज्या छेदेन विभाजिता ।
रवीन्द्वोर्लम्बनं ज्ञेयं प्राक्पश्चाद्घटिकादिकम् ।।
slokas.translit:
madhyalagnārkaviśleṣajyā chedena vibhājitā ।
ravīndvorlambanaṃ jñeyaṃ prākpaścādghaṭikādikam ।।

anvaya.en: मध्यलग्न और सूर्य के अन्तर की ज्या

slokas.translation: The sine of the difference between the madhyalagna (meridian ecliptic point) and the Sun, divided by the cheda, is the lambana of the Sun and the Moon. Take it as eastward or westward, and express it in ghaṭikā and the finer time units.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v5-08 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 5.8)

formula.title: Topocentric Parallax in Longitude & Latitude
formula.notes: Source-bounded summary of 5.3–5.12. The former 4×sin/48×sin shortcut and 5.1–5.40 metadata were generated errors and are retired.

chapters.codeSnippet:
# SS 5.5-5.8 and 5.11 as in the formula above, with the text's sine: its 24 R-sines on R = 3438, read by linear interpolation
JYA = [0, 225, 449, 671, 890, 1105, 1315, 1520, 1719, 1910, 2093, 2267, 2431, 2585, 2728, 2859,
       2978, 3084, 3177, 3256, 3321, 3372, 3409, 3431, 3438]
R = 3438

def jya(deg):
    d = deg % 360
    b, s = (d, 1) if d < 90 else (180 - d, 1) if d < 180 else (d - 180, -1) if d < 270 else (360 - d, -1)
    m = b * 60                                    # arcminutes
    i = min(int(m // 225), 23)
    return s * (JYA[i] + (m - 225 * i) * (JYA[i + 1] - JYA[i]) / 225)

def lambana_nati(natamsa_deg, udayajya, madhya_minus_sun_deg):
    M = jya(natamsa_deg)                          # madhyajyā
    D = (M * M - (M * udayajya / R) ** 2) ** 0.5  # dṛkkṣepa
    G = (R * R - D * D) ** 0.5                    # dṛggati
    C = JYA[8] ** 2 / G                           # cheda: jyā(one sign)² ÷ dṛggati (reading 'ekajyā-varga')
    L = jya(madhya_minus_sun_deg) / C             # lambana, in ghaṭikā
    return {'drkkshepa': round(D, 2), 'drggati': round(G, 2), 'cheda': round(C, 2), 'lambana_ghatika': round(L, 3),
            'nati_arcmin_by_70': round(D / 70, 2), 'nati_arcmin_by_49': round(49 * D / R, 2)}
chapters.codeOutput:
Input (illustrative values, not an observed eclipse): natāṃśa 30°, udayajyā 1500, madhya-lagna − Sun 20°
lambana_nati(30, 1500, 20) → {'drkkshepa': 1546.76, 'drggati': 3070.4, 'cheda': 962.4, 'lambana_ghatika': 1.221, 'nati_arcmin_by_70': 22.1, 'nati_arcmin_by_49': 22.05}
(madhyajyā = jyā 30° = 1719; lambana 1.221 ghaṭikā; nati about 22′ by either rule of 5.11)

chapters.verseRange: Verses 6.1 – 6.24 (24 श्लोक in the edition) · shown here: 6.11

slokas.deva:
विक्षेपाग्राल्लिखेद्वृत्तं ग्राहकार्धेन तेन यत् ।
ग्राह्यवृत्तं समाक्रान्तं तद्ग्रस्तं तमसा भवेत् ।।
slokas.translit:
vikṣepāgrāllikhedvṛttaṃ grāhakārdhena tena yat ।
grāhyavṛttaṃ samākrāntaṃ tadgrastaṃ tamasā bhavet ।।
slokas.translation: From the tip of the vikṣepa draw a circle with radius equal to half the eclipsing body’s diameter. Whatever of the eclipsed body’s circle that circle covers is what is seized by darkness — the geometric definition of the eclipsed portion on the board.

chapters.verseRange: Verses 7.1 – 7.24 (24 श्लोक in the edition) · shown here: 7.18, 7.19
chapters.overview: Calculates geocentric planetary conjunctions (Bhedha, Ullekha, Anshuvimarda, Apasavya), occultations, and mutual distance vectors.

slokas.deva:
स्वशङ्कुमूर्धगौ व्योम्नि ग्रहौ दृक्तुल्यतां इतौ ।
उल्लेखं तारकास्पर्शाद्भेदे भेदः प्रकीर्त्यते ।।
slokas.translit:
svaśaṅkumūrdhagau vyomni grahau dṛktulyatāṃ itau ।
ullekhaṃ tārakāsparśādbhede bhedaḥ prakīrtyate ।।
slokas.translation: The two planets, having attained equality of vision in the sky, are shown at the tops of their respective gnomons. Contact with a star is called ullekha; when they are distinct from each other, the state is named bheda.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v7-18 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 7.18)

slokas.deva:
युद्धं अंशुविमर्दाख्यं अंशुयोगे परस्परम् ।
अंशादूने अपसव्याख्यं युद्धं एको अत्र चेदणुः ।।
slokas.translit:
yuddhaṃ aṃśuvimardākhyaṃ aṃśuyoge parasparam ।
aṃśādūne apasavyākhyaṃ yuddhaṃ eko atra cedaṇuḥ ।।
slokas.translation: Mutual pressing of the rays is the combat named aṃśu-vimarda. When the separation is less than one degree, the combat is called apasavya; and if one of the two is minute (aṇu), that condition belongs here as well.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v7-19 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 7.19)

chapters.verseRange: Verses 8.1 – 8.21 (21 श्लोक in the edition) · shown here: 8.13
chapters.overview: Catalogues the canonical polar longitudes (Dhruvaka) and polar latitudes (Vikshepa) of the 27 junction stars (Yogataras) defining the sidereal ecliptic lattice.

slokas.deva:
वृषे सप्तदशे भागे यस्य याम्यो अंशकद्वयात् ।
विक्षेपो अभ्यधिको भिन्द्याद्रोहिण्याः शकतं तु सः ।।
slokas.translit:
vṛṣe saptadaśe bhāge yasya yāmyo aṃśakadvayāt ।
vikṣepo abhyadhiko bhindyādrohiṇyāḥ śakataṃ tu saḥ ।।
slokas.translation: That body which stands in the seventeenth degree of Taurus, with southern latitude greater than two degrees, is said to split Rohiṇī’s cart. The verse states a geometric gate: longitude window plus a latitude threshold.

chapters.verseRange: Verses 9.1 – 9.18 (18 श्लोक in the edition) · shown here: 9.6, 9.7, 9.8
chapters.overview: Determines the exact visibility threshold angles (Kalabhaga) for planets appearing from or disappearing into the Sun's blinding disk.

slokas.deva:
एकादशामरेज्यस्य तिथिसङ्ख्यार्कजस्य च ।
अस्तांशा भूमिपुत्रस्य दश सप्ताधिकास्ततः ।।
slokas.translit:
ekādaśāmarejyasya tithisaṅkhyārkajasya ca ।
astāṃśā bhūmiputrasya daśa saptādhikāstataḥ ।।
slokas.translation: The heliacal limit-degrees (astāṃśa) are: Jupiter 11°, Saturn 15° (tithi-count), Mars 17° (ten plus seven). These are fixed visibility thresholds for the three outer planets, not rates or periods.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v9-06 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 9.6)

slokas.deva:
पश्चादस्तमयो अष्टाभिरुदयः प्राङ्महत्तया ।
प्रागस्तं उदयः पश्चादल्पत्वाद्दशभिर्भृगोः ।।
slokas.translit:
paścādastamayo aṣṭābhirudayaḥ prāṅmahattayā ।
prāgastaṃ udayaḥ paścādalpatvāddaśabhirbhṛgoḥ ।।
slokas.translation: For Venus: western setting and eastern rising by 8° when “great” (brighter phase); eastern setting and western rising by 10° when “small” (fainter phase). Two thresholds track phase-dependent brilliance.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v9-07 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 9.7)

slokas.deva:
एवं बुधो द्वादशभिश्चतुर्दशभिरंशकैः ।
वक्री शीघ्रगतिश्चार्कात्करोत्यस्तमयोदयौ ।।
slokas.translit:
evaṃ budho dvādaśabhiścaturdaśabhiraṃśakaiḥ ।
vakrī śīghragatiścārkātkarotyastamayodayau ।।
slokas.translation: So Mercury effects setting and rising relative to the Sun by 12° when retrograde and by 14° when in swift (śīghra) motion. The pair of limits closes the fixed-threshold list begun for the outer planets and Venus.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v9-08 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 9.8)

chapters.nameEn: Lunar Horn Elevation & Crescent Phase Geometry
chapters.verseRange: Verses 10.1 – 10.15 (15 श्लोक in the edition) · shown here: 10.9
chapters.overview: Trigonometric derivation of the illuminated lunar phase angle, crescent width (Shukla-Paksha phase), and the tilt/elevation of the northern and southern horns of the Moon.

slokas.deva:
सूर्योनशीतगोर्लिप्ताः शुक्लं नवशतोद्धृताः ।
चन्द्रबिम्बाङ्गुलाभ्यस्तं हृतं द्वादशभिः स्फुटम् ।।
slokas.translit:
sūryonaśītagorliptāḥ śuklaṃ navaśatoddhṛtāḥ ।
candrabimbāṅgulābhyastaṃ hṛtaṃ dvādaśabhiḥ sphuṭam ।।
slokas.translation: Take the minutes of arc of the Moon diminished by the Sun (the elongation). Divided by nine hundred they yield the “white” measure—the illuminated portion in a twelve-part scale. That quantity, multiplied by the Moon’s disk in aṅgulas and divided by twelve, is the true illuminated measure for the moment.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v10-09 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 10.9)

chapters.verseRange: Verses 11.1 – 11.23 (23 श्लोक in the edition) · shown here: 11.1, 11.2
chapters.overview: Mathematical analysis of celestial declination equality (Vaidhruta and Vyatipata), when the Sun and Moon share identical declinations on opposite sides of the celestial equator.

slokas.deva:
एकायनगतौ स्यातां सूर्यचन्द्रमसौ यदा ।
तद्युतौ मण्डले क्रान्त्योस्तुल्यत्वे वैधृताभिधः ।।
slokas.translit:
ekāyanagatau syātāṃ sūryacandramasau yadā ।
tadyutau maṇḍale krāntyostulyatve vaidhṛtābhidhaḥ ।।

anvaya.en: दोनों की क्रान्तियों (विषुवत्-अयन-झुकाव) के समान होने पर

slokas.translation: When the Sun and Moon lie in the same ayan, and in the circle their conjunction is such that their declinations become equal, that condition is named Vaidhṛta. The verse fixes two co-requisites: shared ayan and equal krānti.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v11-01 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 11.1)

slokas.deva:
विपरीतायनगतौ चन्द्रार्कौ क्रान्तिलिप्तिका ।
समास्तदा व्यतीपातो भगणार्धे तयोर्युतौ ।।
slokas.translit:
viparītāyanagatau candrārkau krāntiliptikā ।
samāstadā vyatīpāto bhagaṇārdhe tayoryutau ।।
slokas.translation: When Moon and Sun are in opposite ayans, their declination-minutes are equal, and their conjunction (sum-yuti) stands at half a revolution, that is Vyatīpāta. The half-bhagaṇa fixes the 180° sum against Vaidhṛta’s full-circle meeting.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v11-02 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 11.2)

formula.title: Declination Equivalence Equation
formula.notes: Critical for high-precision institutional astrological and almanac calculations.

chapters.codeSnippet:
def check_vyatipata(sun_dec, moon_dec, tolerance=0.1):
    return abs(abs(sun_dec) - abs(moon_dec)) < tolerance

declination-magnitude difference = 0.0300°

chapters.verseRange: Verses 12.1 – 12.90 (90 श्लोक in the edition) · shown here: 12.32
chapters.overview: Comprehensive geography and cosmography. Establishes the spherical Earth (Bhugola), prime meridian through Ujjayini (75.7885° E), Lanka equatorial zero-point, Meru polar axis, and antipodal coordinates.

slokas.deva:
मध्ये समन्तादण्डस्य भूगोलो व्योम्नि तिष्ठति ।
बिभ्रानः परमां शक्तिं ब्रह्मणो धारणात्मकाम् ।।
slokas.translit:
madhye samantādaṇḍasya bhūgolo vyomni tiṣṭhati ।
bibhrānaḥ paramāṃ śaktiṃ brahmaṇo dhāraṇātmakām ।।
slokas.translation: At the centre of the cosmic egg, on every side, the earth-globe stands in the sky, bearing Brahman’s supreme power whose very nature is to uphold and sustain.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v12-32 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 12.32)

formula.title: Deshantara Longitudinal Time Difference
formula.notes: SS 1.62 names the prime meridian through Laṅkā, Rohītaka and Avantī (Ujjayinī).

chapters.codeSnippet:
def deshantara_time_correction(lon_deg, ujjain_lon=75.7885):
    return (lon_deg - ujjain_lon) * 4.0 # in minutes of time
chapters.codeOutput:
Input: Kāśī longitude 83.0107° E (baseline: Ujjain 75.7885° E)
deshantara_time_correction(83.0107) → +28.8888 minutes of time

chapters.verseRange: Verses 13.1 – 13.25 (25 श्लोक in the edition) · shown here: 13.3, 13.23
chapters.overview: Mechanical engineering blueprints for constructing the Golayantra (armillary sphere), Kapalayantra (clepsydra/water clock), and self-rotating astronomical automatons.

slokas.deva:
भूभगोलस्य रचनां कुर्यादाश्चर्यकारिणीम् ।
अभीष्टं पृथिवीगोलं कारयित्वा तु दारवम् ॥
slokas.translit:
bhūbhagolasya racanāṃ kuryādāścaryakāriṇīm ।
abhīṣṭaṃ pṛthivīgolaṃ kārayitvā tu dāravam ।।
slokas.translation: One should construct a wonder-working model of the earth-and-sky sphere. First fashion a wooden terrestrial globe of the desired size; on that solid body the whole armillary apparatus will rest.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v13-03 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 13.3)

slokas.deva:
ताम्रपात्रं अधश्छिद्रं न्यस्तं कुण्डे अमलाम्भसि ।
षष्टिर्मज्जत्यहोरात्रे स्फुटं यन्त्रं कपालकम् ॥
slokas.translit:
tāmrapātraṃ adhaśchidraṃ nyastaṃ kuṇḍe amalāmbhasi ।
ṣaṣṭirmajjatyahorātre sphuṭaṃ yantraṃ kapālakam ।।
slokas.translation: A copper vessel with a hole beneath, set in a basin of pure water, sinks sixty times in a day-and-night — that is the accurate kapāla instrument.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v13-23 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 13.23)

chapters.nameEn: Reckoning of Time & Eras (Nine Mana Scales)
chapters.verseRange: Verses 14.1 – 14.27 (27 श्लोक in the edition) · shown here: 14.1
chapters.overview: The crowning synthesis of the nine measures of time named in SS 14.1: brāhma, divya, pitrya, prājāpatya, bārhaspatya (guru), saura, sāvana, cāndra and ārkṣa (nākṣatra).

slokas.deva:
ब्राह्मं दिव्यं तथा पित्र्यं प्राजापत्यं गुरोस्तथा ।
सौरं च सावनं चान्द्रं आर्क्षं मानानि वै नव ।।
slokas.translit:
brāhmaṃ divyaṃ tathā pitryaṃ prājāpatyaṃ gurostathā ।
sauraṃ ca sāvanaṃ cāndraṃ ārkṣaṃ mānāni vai nava ।।
slokas.translation: There are nine measures of time: those of Brahmā, of the gods, of the pitṛs, of Prajāpati, of the preceptor (Jupiter), the solar, the civil (sāvana), the lunar, and the sidereal (ārkṣa). The verse simply names the full set before distinguishing which of them govern ordinary reckoning.
slokas.source: editions/surya-siddhanta-full-edition.html#v14-01 — Devanāgarī, IAST, padaccheda-anvaya and English rendering as printed in the edition (सूर्य-सिद्धान्त 14.1)
